# Wave Laboratory: appendix {.page-title}

[Wave models · validation scope · limits]{.kicker}

Supporting notes for the [Wave Laboratory case study](../wave-laboratory.qmd). The counts below are the October 2026 audit snapshot unless a section says otherwise.

## Wave models

| Component | Model |
| --- | --- |
| Energy spectrum | JONSWAP, Pierson–Moskowitz, Bretschneider |
| Shallow water | TMA depth correction |
| Fetch-limited growth | Hasselmann |
| Directional spread | Published spreading functions |
| Dispersion | Finite depth and surface tension |
| Surface synthesis | Four inverse FFT cascades, 1 km to centimetre scales |
| Crest sharpening | Choppy sideways displacement |
| Rogue waves | NewWave focusing |
| Water optics | Jerlov water types, Snell's window |

The GPU and CPU read the same amplitudes; the app compares one texel with the CPU result on each new sea and fails the browser tests if they disagree.

## Validation scope

| Suite | Count at the snapshot |
| --- | ---: |
| Long-running validation tests | 25 in 9 files |
| Unit and component tests | Several hundred declarations; not re-counted here |
| Browser tests | Desktop and mobile Playwright, including axe |

Unit-test declarations are not a passing-test total. The repository's own README badge and the local grep count use different methods, so this appendix reports the validation suite only.

## Reference case

The Draupner crest is the reference: 18.5 m in a sea with 11.9 m significant wave height. The rogue-wave preset targets that shape on purpose.

## What is not modelled

- Current shear with depth and wave refraction by currents.
- Floodwater sloshing inside damaged compartments.
- Certified seakeeping calculations; this is a teaching and exploration tool.
- A WebGPU backend; the shipped renderer is WebGL 2 behind an interface.

## Reproduce

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test
pnpm test:e2e
```

The staged plan's Stokes, cnoidal, Boussinesq and scripting phases are not built.

:::
